summary:
ASTROVA is an interactive educational website that brings the stories of NASA's abandoned and discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars to life. Our project is designed especially for students and young space enthusiasts. Instead of presenting the equipment as simple technical objects, ASTROVA turns their missions, discoveries, locations, and stories into an engaging digital experience.

The website helps users understand what equipment was left behind, why it was important, what science it helped scientists discover, and how these missions contributed to our understanding of the Moon and Mars. Through storytelling, visuals, and an easy-to-use interface, ASTROVA makes space exploration more understandable, memorable, and exciting.

Our goal is to show that equipment left behind is not simply forgotten hardware. Each object represents a mission, a scientific achievement, and a part of humanity's journey beyond Earth.
details:
ASTROVA is a web-based storytelling and educational experience created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten."

The main problem we wanted to address is that young learners may know about famous space missions but may not understand the equipment that remains on the Moon and Mars after missions are completed. These objects can easily be viewed as forgotten hardware, even though they played important roles in exploration and scientific discovery.

Our solution is an interactive website that presents the stories of space equipment in a simple and engaging way. ASTROVA combines storytelling, visuals, space facts, and an easy navigation experience so users can explore the history and purpose of equipment left behind on other worlds.

The target audience is mainly students, school-age space enthusiasts, and anyone who wants to learn about space exploration without needing advanced technical knowledge.

The website experience is designed to make learning feel like an exploration journey. Users can move through the content, learn about the Moon and Mars, discover the purpose of different equipment, and understand how these missions helped scientists collect information.

ASTROVA demonstrates how NASA's mission history and scientific information can be transformed into an accessible educational experience. Our project focuses on storytelling rather than simply listing technical facts, helping users connect the equipment with the people, missions, discoveries, and history behind them.

The project is currently presented as a responsive web experience and can be accessed through the live project link provided above.
